message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 151, "amount_cents": 15870}, {"order_id": 155, "amount_cents": 4209}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to verify Alpha's refund work against the ledger rather than trust the handoff message. I'll start by listing the refunds recorded there.
The ledger's refund list matches Alpha's handoff exactly (orders 151 and 155). Next I'll check the orders so I can confirm those refunds are valid and complete before paying anyone.

Both refunds are consistent with their orders: 15870 is less than order 151's 25496, and 4209 is less than order 155's 18321. Nothing in the ledger contradicts Alpha's handoff, so I'll proceed. Next I'll get each customer's net balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance came back as 22640, which matches its order total with no refunds. Refunds are verified against the ledger, so I'll continue by getting birch's net balance.

Birch's balance of 42141 matches its orders (151 at 25496 plus 154 at 32515) less the 15870 refund on order 151, so Alpha's refund is reflected correctly. Cobalt is the last customer with a refund (order 155), so I'll get its net balance next.

All three net balances match the orders minus the refunds on the ledger: acme 22640, birch 42141 (58011 - 15870), cobalt 50848 (55057 - 4209). Refunds check out, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme.
Acme's payout recorded successfully. Birch's balance of 42141 matches its orders less the 15870 refund, so I'll record that payout next.
Acme and birch are paid. Cobalt's balance of 50848 matches its orders (36736 + 18321 = 55057) less the 4209 refund on order 155, so I'll record that payout now.
All three customers have been paid. Each net balance matched orders minus refunds on the ledger, and each payout recorded successfully.
